name: Composite Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues

criteria.description: Presence of two or more distinct types of lymphoma within the same anatomical site confirmed by histopathological examination
Immunophenotypic evidence demonstrating distinct clonal populations corresponding to different lymphoma subtypes
Molecular or cytogenetic studies confirming clonally unrelated lymphoid populations
Clinical presentation consistent with lymphoma including lymphadenopathy or extranodal masses

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of two distinct lymphoma types in the same lesion with immunophenotypic and/or molecular evidence of clonally unrelated populations
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of histology, immunophenotyping, and molecular studies to distinguish composite lymphoma from transformed or composite variants.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Coexistence of two distinct lymphoma histologies in a single biopsy specimen
searchTerms: two types of lymphoma cells in one biopsy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Simultaneous lymphadenopathy with heterogeneous histopathological features
searchTerms: enlarged lymph nodes with mixed cell types
lymph node swelling with varied pathology

common.symptomName: B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)

searchTerms: symptoms from low red blood cells
fatigue and pale skin from anemia
tiredness and pallor due to anemia

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to CNS involvement
searchTerms: neurological symptoms from brain or spinal involvement
nerve problems due to central nervous system disease
brain or spinal cord related neurological signs

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to lymphomatous infiltration

laboratory: Abnormal peripheral blood smear in some cases
imaging: CT or PET-CT showing lymphadenopathy with heterogeneous lesions
genetic: Distinct clonal rearrangements in immunoglobulin or T-cell receptor genes for each lymphoma component
Cytogenetic abnormalities specific to each lymphoma subtype
other: Histopathological evidence of two morphologically and immunophenotypically distinct lymphomas in the same tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Single lymphoma subtype with transformation to a higher grade
Clonal relationship between initial and transformed lymphoma cells
Presence of both Hodgkin lymphoma and non-Hodgkin lymphoma components
Distinct immunophenotypic markers differentiating Hodgkin Reed-Sternberg cells

redFlags: Evidence of multiple distinct lymphoma populations on biopsy
references: Swerdlow SH, Campo E, Harris NL, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues. IARC; 2017.
Jaffe ES. Composite lymphoma: a diagnostic challenge. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2016;30(6):1239-1252.
